title: Learning bass and playing with Earl Foster
summary: He learned to watch bass players, played in Earl Foster's four-piece band, and recalls the night he played bass for Chester Zardis.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well I liked that from being on Boots, Austin Young, an old man named Austin Young. I used to watch the way he played his bass, you know. But I played with Earl Foster during that time. We had a... In fact, Earl Foster's on there, he had the first four piece band in the city. They had Willie Jam, Louis Jam's brother. That's, of course, both of them did. Willie did too. Now, Louis Jam and another, ain't no way than Willie, but they had another jam. I was playing with you. Boots played a bass. Joe Harris played saxophone.
Joe Harris plays with you sometimes, whenever you couldn't get capped.
Well Joe Harris took Willie Jam and played after he went to California.

I have a picture of you playing a bass in the tux. One night you and Chester's artists were playing somewhere, and you couldn't make it. That gig wasn't going to be over until about nine, and Charlie Hamilton sat in, remember?
Yeah, I came with my brother.
And you got there first, and Chester wasn't there, so they played without a bass. And then you played the bass for about three numbers, and then Chester showed up, and I got a shot of you.
You got that picture? Yeah, I got it on the coastline.
You haven't seen this one. I can't. But I remember I said, boy, I was glad I had the camera that night, because you came in, and you—
Well, we played for Sonny. That's what we played that night. Oh yeah? We played for Sonny.
Sonny from Carolina. Yeah, we played for them that night.

Yeah. We played for Roseville, because— One of those runners, yeah, we played for Roseville. In other words, Chester and I was the Grand Marchion, and the band came in playing by me, Chester. Oh. See, and I had the back of the bass, the front of the bass, going to the bandstand. And when we got to the bandstand, I got on the piano while he tuned his bass up and made like that, and we still ran him in, and started playing. Well, then you brought—but you brought the bass with you when you came? I brought the band, yeah, I brought the bass with you. How come you didn't come together that night? Oh what? Chester had to go in and park the car. Oh, I see, that's what it wanted to be. Chester had to go in and park the car. Chester had to go in and park the car. Oh, I see, that's what it wanted to be.
